# x a of two limbs, a of T

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `scale_step_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An approximation $z$ of $x a$:

$$z \approx x a.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x = x_0 + x_1$, $z = z_0 + z_1$.

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of the loop `bv_scale_2`, called by `x * a`, `a * x`, `x *= a`, `scale(x, a, z)` and `axpy` of `BallVector<T, 2, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 2>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $x$ is normalized: $x_0 = \mathrm{RN}(x_0 + x_1)$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $z$ is normalized: $z_0 = \mathrm{RN}(z_0 + z_1)$.
- $\lvert z - x a\rvert \le 2\,u^2\,\lvert x a\rvert + \eta$.

The constants of the bound, for each limb type, from `gen/claims.json`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| unit roundoff $u$ | $2^{-53}$ | $2^{-24}$ |
| relative term $c\,u^2$ | $2^{-105} \approx 2.4652 \times 10^{-32}$ | $2^{-47} \approx 7.1054 \times 10^{-15}$ |
| absolute term $t\,\eta$ | $2^{-1074} \approx 4.9407 \times 10^{-324}$ | $2^{-149} \approx 1.4013 \times 10^{-45}$ |
| `unit`, `tiny`, as compiled | `0x1p-105`, `0x1p-1074` | `0x1p-47f`, `0x1p-149f` |
| `unit_computed`, `tiny_computed` | `0x1.0000000000001p-105`, `0x1p-1073` | `0x1.000002p-47f`, `0x1p-148f` |

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `scale_step_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/MapSteps.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/MapSteps.v), against `scale_step_2_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions scale_step_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition scale_step_2_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (2 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall x0 x1 a : R,
  normalized_2 emin prec x0 x1 ->
  fmt emin prec a ->
  let '(z0, z1) := scale_step_2 emin prec tie_even x0 x1 a in
  normalized_2 emin prec z0 z1 /\
  Rabs ((z0 + z1) - ((x0 + x1) * a)) <= 2 * u prec ^ 2 * Rabs ((x0 + x1) * a) + 1 * eta emin.
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `scale_step_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** mul_2_1 ([JMP17](../developer/design/phase0/references.md#jmp17) Alg. 9, DWTimesFP3); bound from [MR22](../developer/design/phase0/references.md#mr22). **License:** algorithm: published; proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/scale_step_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/scale_step_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`mul_2_1`](mul_2_1.md).

```
# The step of the map scale_2, an array of two limbs times a scalar of T: mul_2_1 (milestone2.md:
# mul_2_1 when the scalar of scale is a T). Both come from the program; mul_2_1 only multiplies
# them, so rule R3 asks no guard. Its claims are those of mul_2_1.

(z0, z1) = mul_2_1(x0, x1, a)
```

## Measured

No stored brute-force run has judged this kernel yet.

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only limbs given by the program can make: `from_limbs` in a build without checks, `from_limbs_unchecked`, or `limb[]` written directly.
